claim: The reusable Canvas glyph shadow is composited behind existing canvas ink, then the original glyph is drawn once. At the tested viewport-derived units this retains shadow support without changing already-opaque glyph colour.

evidence.pixel_comparison: Actual SpriteSheet native canvas at 1280x800 and 390x844: respectively 29,664 and 12,617 shadow-only support pixels; opaque glyph samples differed by at most one UNORM unit from no-shadow; source pixels were identical before global inversion.
evidence.software_gles: The existing readable_contract from w/display/w/wy/locus-shader.gles.test.py passed separately at 1280x800 and 390x844, using actual captured locus-shader commands on software GLES. It checked sharp foreground, retained shadow, focused background blur, overlapping reading surfaces and refracted header/compass surfaces.
evidence.mobile: The mobile-reading step of the linked run passed 24 combinations: six sites, DE/EN and 320x568/390x844, with emulated touch. Its next long-axis step passed 12 cases and live turns. The overall workflow later failed at the obsolete membrane fit assertion, so its other later browser suites are not claimed.

limits: The combined full local locus-shader.gles.test.py process exited 137 in this environment after the initial change; the two readable_contract executions above are narrower evidence, not a full-suite pass.
No physical GPU, physical touch device, full global format migration, selected Source interaction, or deployment is claimed.
